mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.2% indicate a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with falling inflation, which may signal a policy pivot and support positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.2% in the same month
regime_hint: policy pivot from tightening to neutral
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decrease in the unemployment rate below 4% and an increase in average hourly earnings (PAYEMS per capita) above 0.3% indicate a tight labor market with upward wage pressure, which raises input costs and may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND PAYEMS per capita growth > 0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 900 thousand units for three consecutive months signals a weakening housing market, which reduces construction-related economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).
